+title: undo(txn:) on a transaction that is already undone
+---
+## What
+`Sources/FoundationModelsKanban/Undo/UndoLog.swift:93-96` (`target(named:)`) does not check `isUndone`. In the conflict check (`:198-205`), the earlier undo `U` of `T` counts as a later change. Thus `undo(txn: T)` after `T` is undone gives `UNDO_CONFLICT` that names `U`, and with `force: true` it writes a second undo of `T`.
+
+- In `target(named:)`, when the target is already undone, give a clear error. Use the existing nothing-to-undo error code if there is one; if not, add `ALREADY_UNDONE` to plan.md §4.4 and to the code enum. `force: true` does not override this error.
+- The same check for `redo(txn:)` on a transaction that is not undone.
+- Update plan.md §6.5.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `undo(txn: T)` two times: the second call gives the "already undone" error and writes nothing, also with `force: true`.
+- [ ] `redo(txn: T)` when `T` is not undone gives a clear error and writes nothing.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Tests in `Tests/FoundationModelsKanbanTests/Undo/`.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
